Two Democratic senators who have long overseen US intelligence say the Trump administration is illegally withholding a secret court’s findings from Congress until lawmakers renew a program that lets federal agents read Americans’ communications without a warrant.

两位长期监督美国情报机构的民主党参议员表示，特朗普政府非法向国会扣留一家秘密法庭的认定结果，直至议员们续授一项允许联邦探员在无授权令情况下阅读美国人通信内容的计划。

Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires. The court approved another year of surveillance anyway. The ruling has never been made public, and Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Adam Schiff of California say the administration’s own deadline for releasing it passed in September.

七个月前，外国情报监控法院反对使用搜索过滤器，允许情报分析员在未经法律要求的审批、书面理由或记录的情况下，从拦截的数据中提取美国人的信息。尽管如此，该法院仍批准继续进行一年监视。该裁决从未公开，俄勒冈州参议员罗恩·怀登和加州参议员亚当·施夫表示，政府发布该裁决的截止日期在9月已经过去。

The program, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), lapsed in June after Congress failed to renew it, though collection continues under the court’s March approval. The administration’s own public documentation says rulings like this one are reviewed for public release “within 180 days of issuance.” That window closed September 13, even as intelligence officials press lawmakers to reauthorize the program by the end of the year.

该程序，Section 702 的外国情报监控法 (FISA)，于六月在国会未能续期后失效，尽管收集工作在法院三月的批准下继续进行。行政当局的[自己的公开文档]表示，此类裁决在公开发布时会在“发布后 180 天内”进行审查。该时间窗口于 9 月 13 日关闭，尽管情报官员正在敦促立法者在年底前重新授权该程序。

Wyden, the longest-serving member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, and Schiff, the former chair of its House counterpart, say the administration owes Congress an explanation for the delay, and the names of the officials responsible, by November 6.

参议院情报委员会资历最深的成员 Wyden，以及该委员会众议院对应机构的前主席 Schiff 表示，政府欠国会一个关于延迟原因的解释，以及相关负责官员的名单，截止日期为 11 月 6 日。

“If this administration won’t follow this simple statutory directive,” the senators told Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Attorney General Todd Blanche in a demand letter obtained exclusively by WIRED, “it is unclear why Congress or the American people should trust this administration to follow any of the other legal limits to Section 702.”

“如果政府不遵守这项简单的法定指令，”参议员们在一份致国家情报总监 Jay Clayton 和司法部长 Todd Blanche 的要求信（由 WIRED 独家获得）中写道，“国会或美国民众就不清楚为何应信任该政府会遵守第 702 条的其他任何法律限制。”

Outside Congress, Demand Progress and 22 other civil liberties and government accountability groups on Monday urged congressional leaders to refuse to reauthorize Section 702 “while the administration actively withholds legally mandated information about how the surveillance program operates.” Signatories range from the American Civil Liberties Union to the conservative-backed Project for Privacy and Surveillance Accountability.

在国会大楼外，众大的进步组织（Demand Progress）以及 22 家其他民事自由和政府问责团体周一敦促国会领袖拒绝重新授权第 702 条款的《FISCDeadline.pdf》（https://www.demandprogress.org/api/media/file/FISCDeadline.pdf），理由是“在行政部门积极隐藏法律要求提供的有关监视计划运作方式的信息之际。”签署支持者从美国民事自由联盟（ACLU）到保守派支持的“隐私与监视问责项目”（Project for Privacy and Surveillance Accountability）等组织均包含其中。

The Trump administration has already been pressed, and has promised, to release the ruling. In April, senators Tom Cotton and Mark Warner, the Intelligence Committee’s Republican chair and Democratic vice chair, pressed the administration to release it within 15 days so it could inform the Senate’s debate. In July, asked in writing whether he would commit to declassifying it by the 180-day deadline, Blanche replied, “Yes.”

特朗普政府此前已受到施压，并已承诺公布该裁决。4 月，参议员汤姆·科顿和马克·沃纳——情报委员会的共和党主席和民主党副主席——施压政府，要求其在 15 天内公布，以便为参议院的辩论提供参考。7 月，在书面询问他是否承诺在 180 天期限内将其解密时，布兰奇回答：“是的。”

Warner “has been clear that he supports transparency with regard to Section 702,” his communications director, Rachel Cohen, tells WIRED. Neither former director of national intelligence Tulsi Gabbard nor Bill Pulte, who briefly replaced her as acting director, “were responsive,” Cohen says, “but Senator Warner expects that DNI Clayton will declassify the opinion, consistent with the bipartisan letter and as required by law.”

温纳德表示，他一直明确支持关于第702条的透明度，“他的通讯主任拉切尔·科恩告诉WIRED。” 图尔西·加巴德（前国家情报局局长）和比尔·普尔特（曾短暂接替她担任代理局长），“没有回应，“科恩说，“但参议员温纳德期望DNI克莱顿将解密该意见，符合两党信函的要求以及法律规定。

Cotton’s office did not respond to a request for comment. The White House, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and the US Justice Department did not answer questions WIRED sent Friday about the delay.

Cotton’s 办公室未对评论请求作出回应。White House， Office of the Director of National Intelligence，和 US Justice Department未就 WIRED 于周五 发送的问题 回答 关于延迟。

Clayton, who is legally responsible as director of national intelligence for declassifying the ruling, has made no such promise. Asked before his July confirmation whether he would ensure the opinion was public before Congress voted on reauthorization, he wrote only that the government was “working arduously to expeditiously declassify” it and had made the full opinion available to lawmakers.

Clayton 作为国家情报总监依法负责解密该裁决，但并未作出此类承诺。在 7 月的确认听证会前，当被问及是否会确保该法律意见在国会就重新授权进行表决前公开时，他仅写道，政府正在“全力以赴、加快解密”该意见，并已向立法者提供了完整的意见全文。

Some of what the court found is already known. A FISA court opinion declassified last year described a similar FBI tool, a “participants filter” that let agents select people in contact with surveillance targets and read their messages. In February 2025, the Justice Department’s National Security Division told the court the tool had been running searches no one counted. The FBI shut it off the next month and switched it back on later that year, after the department approved a rebuilt version.

法院发现的内容一部分已为人所知。一份已于去年解密的FISA 法院意见“participants filter” 描述了类似的FBI 工具，该工具允许特工选择与监控目标保持联系的人并阅读其信息。2025年2月，Justice Department National Security Division 告诉法院，该工具 had been running 无人统计的搜索。FBI 在下个月关闭了该工具，并在同年稍后 switched it back on later that year，之后部门批准了重建版本。

This year’s ruling went beyond that. The court found that tools agencies use to narrow intercepted data to an American’s messages amount to searches of Americans, subject to the same limits, and ordered them rebuilt, The New York Times reported in April, citing unclassified administration talking points sent to lawmakers. Senator Alex Padilla said in a written question to Blanche that the Justice Department “is appealing portions” of the ruling “limiting the government’s use of certain filtering tools.”

今年的裁决超越了这一点。法院认定，政府机构用来将拦截数据缩小到美国公民消息范围的工具，构成对美国人的搜查，应受到相同的限制，并下令重新构建这些工具。《纽约时报》4月报道称，此消息源自发送给立法者的未分类的政府发言稿。帕迪拉参议员在书面问答中问询布兰奇时表示，司法部正在“上诉限制政府使用某些过滤工具的裁议”。

While the ruling stayed secret, seven intelligence agency fact sheets from March 2026, one dated the day of the ruling, cited a 98.9 percent compliance rate for FBI searches of Americans and credited Section 702 with stopping a planned terrorist attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. None mentions the court’s findings. The figure appears nowhere in the Justice Department inspector general’s October 2025 review of those searches, which put the compliance rate at 98.6 percent and could not conclude that “the FBI’s querying compliance issues are entirely in the past.”

在裁决保持保密期间，2026年3月的七份情报机构数据表中，有一份 dated the day of the ruling（裁决当天的日期标注），引用了FBI对美国公民搜索的98.9%合规率，并称Section 702令其阻止了一起计划袭击维也纳塔拉·斯威特特音乐会的恐怖袭击。None mentions the court’s findings.该数据表中没有一份提到法院发现的表格。该数据在司法部总监长2025年10月的审查报告中未出现，该报告将合规率置于98.6%，并且无法得出结论“FBI的查询合规问题完全已过去”。

According to the fact sheets, FBI auditors review every such search. FBI director Kash Patel closed the bureau’s Office of Internal Auditing last May and moved its auditors into another division. The bureau’s search counts before 2025 also omit queries run through the participants filter, searches the government’s own privacy watchdog says are “not possible to track.”

根据事实资料，FBI 审计员会审查每一次此类搜查。FBI 局长 Kash Patel 于去年 5 月关闭了该局的内部审计办公室，并将其审计员调至另一个部门。该局 2025 年之前的搜查统计数据也未包含通过参与者过滤器 运行的查询，政府自家的隐私监督机构指出，这些搜查“无法追踪”。

Lawmakers who have read the ruling hint that it says more. Senator Dick Durbin, the top Democrat on the Judiciary Committee, urged colleagues on the Senate floor in June to read it in a secure room. “I have seen it,” he said. Once they did, he told them, “your opinion of the role of FISA and the rights of Americans will be impacted for sure.”

已阅读该裁决的立法者暗示，其内容远不止于此。参议院司法委员会资深民主党参议员迪克·德宾 在 6 月的参议院议程上 敦促同僚在保密室内阅读该文件。“我看过它了，”他说道。他告诉他们，一旦读过，“你们对 FISA（外国情报监视法）的作用以及美国民众权利的看法，肯定会受到影响。”

Wyden has also warned about a classified interpretation of Section 702 that he says multiple administrations have relied on and refused to declassify. “When it is eventually declassified,” he said in March, “the American people are going to be stunned that it took so long and that Congress had been debating this authority with insufficient information.”

韦登还警告称，关于《第 702 条》的一个机密解释，据他称多届政府均依赖此解释并拒绝解密。“等到最终解密时，”他在 3 月表示，“美国民众将会震惊，震惊于这拖延了如此之久，以及国会竟在信息不足的情况下辩论这一授权。”

The Trump administration has until November 6 to answer the senators. The court’s current approval of the program expires in March.

特朗普政府在11月6日前须答复参议员。法院对该项目的当前批准将于3月到期。

Surveillance reform advocates say the administration may try to avoid that fight by attaching a renewal to the annual defense authorization bill, which Congress usually finalizes in December. In 2023, lawmakers extended Section 702 for four months through that year’s defense bill after a Senate effort to strip the provision failed. This year’s House and Senate versions of the bill do not yet include it.

监督改革的倡导者表示，政府可能试图回避较量，通过将续签条款附加到年度国防授权法案上来规避它，而国会通常在12月敲定该法案。2023年，立法者在参议院尝试剥夺该条款未果后，通过当年的国防法案将第 702 节延长了四个月。该法案今年众议院和参议院的版本目前尚未包含该条款。将第 702 节延长四个月。

Python’s experimental just-in-time (JIT) compiler, which was added to CPython in 2024 for the 3.13 release, is on its way out. In June, the Python steering council announced that it was pausing work on the JIT in CPython’s main branch until there was an accepted Python Enhancement Proposal (PEP) that addressed concerns about maintenance, compatibility, and set clear success metrics as well as a timeline for completion. After creating PEP 836 (“JIT Go Brrr: The Path to a Supported JIT Compiler for CPython”) to try to meet the council’s request, and after months of discussion, the JIT maintainers have withdrawn the PEP. For now, it appears that development on the once-promising project has come to an end.

Python的实验性即时编译器，该编译器于2024年为3.13版本发布添加到CPython中，正逐渐走向淘汰。6月，Python指导委员会宣布 将在CPython主分支上暂停JIT开发，直到有一个被接受的Python增强提案 (PEP) 解决维护、兼容性问题并设定明确的成功指标以及完成时间表。创建PEP 836（“JIT Go Brrr: The Path to a Supported JIT Compiler for CPython”）以试图满足委员会的要求后，经过数月讨论，JIT维护者已撤回该PEP。目前看来，这一曾经充满希望的项目的开发已经结束。

The JIT was added to CPython by Brandt Bucher in early 2024. Generally, such a major feature would be expected to land only after the council had approved a standards-track PEP. Bucher had given a talk (YouTube video, slides) about the JIT at a Python core developer sprint, and announced his intent to merge the feature—but he had not taken the step of authoring or submitting a PEP for its approval. He was prodded into doing so by steering council member Thomas Wouters, who was also serving as the release manager for Python 3.13.

PEP it up

Work on the JIT had been proceeding on the basis of PEP 744 until this June, when the council had put forward its formal request for the JIT maintainers to create a standards-track PEP. One might wonder, as Antoine Pitrou did, why the council had decided that it was time to speak up and ask for a new PEP. Wouters said that there was no “single triggering event for this request”, but that the council had been discussing the topic for a while and indicated that it was looking to ensure the JIT work did not interfere with other projects. “There’s been work trying to get the JIT to play nice with instrumentation, debugging, and profiling. There’s also external JITs (like CinderX), JIT-adjacent things (like Numba and PyTorch’s compile), and discussions about a tier 3 JIT.” The council had waited until after the Python 3.15 beta release “to be clear that we’re OK with the status quo for 3.15”.

Withdrawn

撤回

After some consideration, it appears, the PEP’s authors have decided not to continue pursing the council’s approval. On October 19, Ostrowski (who is also release manager for Python 3.16 and 3.17) announced that the PEP was being withdrawn:

The Steering Council rightly sets a high bar for a proposal of this scope, and we don’t feel we have the personal bandwidth to carry the current version forward. We continue to believe in the technical direction outlined in the PEP, including free-threaded support and a method-based frontend, and remain optimistic about the JIT’s potential in CPython. We’ll make the reference implementation available and link it from the withdrawn PEP so others who are interested can explore and build on that.

ballombe · 2026-10-26

PyPy 的优势是什么？

acarno · 2026-10-27

首先，PyPy 仅支持 Python 3.12、3.11 和 2.7。更重要的是，PyPy 不是 CPython，它是一个基本兼容但存在一些明显差异的替代实现（PyPy 网站列出了这些差异）。这将直接在 CPython（参考实现）中添加一个 JIT 编译器，从而使所有新的 Python 版本及其所有内置模块都能获得 JIT 编译功能。正如 PEP 836 作者所言：

替代 Python 实现（如 PyPy 和 GraalPy）表明，对于某些 Python 程序，较大的加速是可能的，我们非常重视这些项目。然而，许多用户即使在某些代码上可能获得更好的性能，也无法采用替代运行时，因为存在支持的 Python 版本、扩展兼容性、嵌入要求、部署限制和工具支持等因素限制。

markkitt · 2026-10-27

PyPy 目前处于低维护状态。

LtWorf · 2026-10-27

如果他们拥有与 CPython 相同的资金支持……

marcH · 2026-10-27

Experimentation in main?

> Experimentation in main

Apologies if I missed it: why was this happening in the main branch? Too many conflicts with other changes also happening in main? (Not enough to justify IMHO but that could explain)

> [a compatibility review] that would involve running the test suites of the top PyPI packages to see if the JIT broke them. The council wanted that timeline moved up significantly. “We think that [Aug. 2028] is way, way too late, and the compatibility review should be an ongoing and continuous process starting as soon as possible”.

Maybe I’m missing something again but that seems normal and expected for the main branch - even when not enabled by default.

I didn’t experience it much personally but regressions (in main releases) sound like a relatively frequent complaint about Python…

mathstuf · 2026-10-27

I think it is possible, but the use needs to have a signal that the user knows they’re “playing with fire”. The way we do this for CMake is that there is a variable which needs to be set to a specified value (a randomly generated UUID) for the experiment to become “active” (and its first usage will trigger a warning about it becoming active). If the value is not correct, the feature is ignored. We then change the expected value whenever we update the behavior. With that, projects can’t use the “but the value worked last time!” excuse. Basically, we use it as a way to escape Hyrum’s Law and committing to any in-progress behavior in the future.

marcH · 2026-10-27

Regularly changing the UUID is really cool, this sort of “light-weight branching” is smart! Perfect for letting any user help with testing.

However I can imagine a JIT implementation being “invasive” enough that it “leaks” some changes outside the scope of such an experimental flag. So that technique could still not be completely bullet proof in such a case (it should still be known and used).

The devil is always in the details…

danilo · 2026-10-27

I would say that it was mostly accidental “whoopsie” of allowing active, core contributors to basically side-step the usual process for architectural changes such as this one. Board — once they realised — acted amicably to put things in order, but by that time, JIT work has slowed down sufficiently that it depended on a few contributors with limited bandwidth and they could not commit to address all the concerns and put things back on track.

marcH · 2026-10-27

在 main 分支中进行实验？

> 在 main 分支中进行实验

如果我漏掉了什么，请见谅：为什么这会在 main 分支中发生？与 main 分支中同时进行的其他更改有太多冲突？（恕我直言，这不足以成为理由，但或许可以解释得通）

> [兼容性审查]，这将涉及运行 PyPI 上顶级软件包的测试套件，以查看 JIT 是否破坏了它们。委员会希望显著提前该时间表。“我们认为 [2028 年 8 月] 实在是太晚了，而且兼容性审查应该是一个从尽快开始的持续、连续的过程”。

也许我又漏掉了什么，但这对于 main 分支来说似乎是正常且预期的——即使在默认未启用的情况下也是如此。

我个人没有经历过太多，但回归问题（在 main 版本中）听起来像是对 Python 相当频繁的投诉……

mathstuf · 2026-10-27

我认为这是可能的，但用户需要有一个信号，让他们知道自己正在“玩火”。我们在 CMake 中的做法是，需要将一个变量设置为指定的值（随机生成的 UUID），实验才会变得“活跃”（并且其首次使用会触发关于其变为活跃状态的警告）。如果该值不正确，则忽略该功能。当我们更新行为时，我们随后会更改预期值。这样一来，项目就不能使用“但该值上次有效！”这样的借口。基本上，我们用它作为一种方式来规避 Hyrum’s Law，并避免未来对任何进行中的行为做出承诺。

marcH · 2026-10-27

定期更改 UUID 真的很酷，这种“轻量级分支”很聪明！非常适合让任何用户帮助进行测试。

然而，我可以想象 JIT 实现会具有足够“侵入性”，以至于将某些更改“泄漏”到此类实验标志的范围之外。因此，在这种情况下，该技术可能仍然不完全万无一失（但它仍然应该被知晓并使用）。

魔鬼总是在细节中……

danilo · 2026-10-27

我会说，这主要是意外的“失误”，允许活跃的核心贡献者基本上绕过了此类架构更改的常规流程。委员会（Board）一旦意识到这一点，就友好地采取行动理顺了局面，但到那时，JIT 工作已经放缓到依赖于少数带宽有限的贡献者，他们无法致力于解决所有问题并让事情重回正轨。

roc · 2026-10-27

one problem is Python itself

An underlying problem here seems to be that writing a proper JIT for Python is incredibly hard and the performance gains are pretty small. If the JIT was a runaway success presumably getting the paperwork right would have been less important or at least more people would have helped.

jch · 2026-10-28

> writing a proper JIT for Python is incredibly hard

Harder than for JavaScript? Ruby? Lua? Smalltalk? We’ve got fine JITs for all of these languages, and they are just as dynamic as Python.

raven667 · 2026-10-28

I don’t have any particular insight into the Python internals, but I think the fact that CPython doesn’t have a JIT after all these years and all the available developer hours put into maintenance and features is strong (but anecdotal) evidence that it’s harder than it looks to build a JIT that is compatible with the runtime and the way it’s used/embedded/extended.

ROC · 2026-10-27

一个问题在于 Python 本身

这里似乎存在一个根本问题：为 Python 编写正常的 JIT 编译器几乎不可能，而性能提升其实并不大。如果 JIT 编译器能够大放异彩，可能的话后续的工作量或许会变得不那么重要，或者至少会有更多人愿意投身其中。

jch · 2026-10-28

> 为 Python 编写正常的 JIT 编译器几乎不可能

比 JavaScript、Ruby、Lua、Smalltalk 更难吗？我们为这些语言都拥有出色的 JIT 编译器，它们与 Python 一样都极其动态。

raven667 · 2026-10-28

我对 Python internals 没有特别的见解，但我认为 CPython 已经历了这么多年，花费了这么多可用的开发者时间用于维护和功能开发，仍然没有 JIT 编译器，这本身就强有力的（尽管是概念性的）证据表明：为兼容运行时及其用法/嵌套/扩展方式构建 JIT 编译器，实际上比表面上看起来要难得多。

item.content:encoded:
from: Inside Wikipedia’s Cleanup Effort Against AI Text

Ellia Lebleu is a cofounder of the WikiProject AI Cleanup effort to keep Wikipedia human-written.

Ellia Lebleu 是 WikiProject AI Cleanup 的联合创始人，旨在保持 Wikipedia 人工撰写。

Stuart Bradford

斯图尔特·布拉德福德

Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup, a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove AI-generated material from Wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia.

Ellia Lebleu 是 the WikiProject AI Cleanup 的创始成员，一个于 2023 年启动的志愿者项目，旨在查找和移除 Wikipedia 违反其指南的 AI 生成的材料。清理工作开始时，AI writing 常常因明显的陈词滥调而露馅。如今，该项目的志愿者们正在开发工具来检测更微妙的机器生成内容，并就人工智能在世界上最广泛使用的百科全书中的作用展开辩论。

When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material?

你何时意识到Wikipedia 对 AI 生成的材料存在问题？

Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage.” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this.

埃利亚·勒布勒（Ellia Lebleu）： 那大约是在 2023 年 12 月。我和其他几位编辑在维基百科的 Discord 服务器上聊天，我们都看到了一些具有相同奇特特征的非常奇怪的文章。它们重复着诸如“stands as a testament”或“rich cultural heritage”之类的短语。它们有时还会有结论部分，或者像“Why is this important?”这样的章节。这在 2023 年和 2024 年初的 ChatGPT 中非常典型，但对于维基百科文章来说却非常奇怪——而且很容易被发现。然后我决定，让我们在维基百科上创建一个官方项目，以便更多人来处理这个问题。

Ellia Lebleu

埃利亚·勒布勒

Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph.D. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes, part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology.

Ellia Lebleu 是 WikiProject AI Cleanup 的创始成员。她正在法国国家数字科学与技术研究所（Inria）下属的 雷恩大学 Inria 中心 pursuit a Ph.D. in AI.

How do editors spot AI-generated writing today?

当今编辑如何识别 AI 生成的写作？

Lebleu: By 2025, the signs of AI writing were becoming subtler and more structural. For example, AI loves the “rule of three,” negative parallelisms, and other structures of speech that aren’t conclusive by themselves but become meaningful as they accumulate. We also look beyond the article. If someone writes five articles of thousands of words each in 5 minutes, there is reason to suspect AI.

Lebleu： 到2025 年时，AI 写作的迹象变得更加微妙和结构化。例如，AI 喜欢“三段式法则”、负向平行结构以及其他单独来看并不明显，但随着累积却逐渐显露出意义的语言结构。我们也会超越单篇文章来进行判断。如果某个人在 5 分钟内写了 5 篇数千字的文章，那么就有理由怀疑这可能是 AI 的写作。

Does the AI problem just appear in the main text, or also in citations?

AI 问题仅出现在正文中，还是也出现在引用中？

Lebleu: Fake or misleading citations have become a major worry. Sometimes an AI hallucinates a citation entirely, although that’s much rarer today because of retrieval-augmented generation that allows the AI to find sources. More often, it finds a real source but gets its content completely wrong. AI citations that don’t actually support what is being written are extremely commonplace.

Lebleu: 虚假或误导性引用已成为一大担忧。有时 AI 会完全幻觉出一个引用，但由于 retrieval-augmented generation 让 AI 能够找到来源，这种情况今天已少得多。更常见的是，它找到了一个真实来源，但完全弄错了其内容。那些并不实际支持正在撰写内容的 AI 引用极为普遍。

English Wikipedia recently prohibited editors from using LLMs to generate articles. How much AI-generated content is still getting through?

英文维基百科最近禁止编辑使用 LLM 生成文章。还有多少 AI 生成的内容仍在通过？

Lebleu: I’ve been working with [AI-detection company] Pangram to estimate the proportion of AI-generated content. I tested it on Wikipedia content from before ChatGPT and found no false positives, so its results provide a very conservative lower bound. In late 2025, it flagged perhaps 20 percent of new articles and drafts as AI-generated. In early 2026, that went down to 15 or 16 percent. But we don’t yet know whether that’s because our recent policies have had an effect or because models are getting more powerful and Pangram hasn’t had time to adapt.

Lebleu: 我一直在与 [AI 检测公司] Pangram 合作，估算人工智能生成内容的比例。我在 ChatGPT 出现之前的维基百科内容上测试了它，没有发现误报，因此其结果提供了一个非常保守的下限。在 2025 年晚些时候，它将大约 20% 的新文章和草稿标记为 AI 生成的内容。在 2026 年初，这一比例下降到 15% 或 16%。但我们尚不知道这是因为我们最近的政策产生了影响，还是因为模型变得更强大了，而 Pangram 还没有时间跟上。

Is Wikipedia using AI to combat AI?

Wikipedia 是否在用 AI 对抗 AI？

Lebleu: Another Wikipedia editor has made an AI source verifier, which goes through the sources on a page and checks whether they match the claims. Since it is itself an AI model, there is no guarantee that it will be correct every time. But if you want something that works at scale and filters out obvious cases, it’s a good first step. The Wikimedia Foundation is also working on a tool called Paste Check, which can flag text pasted directly from some AI chatbots.

Lebleu： 另一位 Wikipedia 编辑开发了一个 AI 来源验证器，它会逐一检查页面上的来源，并核实它们是否与声明相符。由于它本身就是一个 AI 模型，无法保证每次都正确。但如果你需要能够大规模运作并过滤掉明显情况的工具，这是一个不错的第一步。Wikimedia 基金会也在开发名为 Paste Check 的工具，它可以标记直接从某些 AI chatbots 粘贴的文本。

And we’ve seen Claude sometimes say, “I can’t write a Wikipedia article; it would go against Wikipedia’s policies.” If all major AI companies implemented that kind of prompt refusal, it wouldn’t solve the problem entirely, because there are still open-weight models that can be tweaked to avoid restrictions. But it would help with people who use commercial models and aren’t especially familiar with the technology.

我们有时会看到 Claude 回答说：“我不能编写维基百科文章，这违反了维基百科的政策。”如果所有主要 AI 公司都能采取这种拒绝执行提示的做法，问题或许仍无法完全解决，因为仍然存在可以被调整以绕过限制的开源权重模型。但这将对那些不熟悉技术的商业模型用户有所帮助。

Can you tell if the rule prohibiting AI writing is working?

你能判断出禁止 AI 写作的规则是否起作用了吗？

Lebleu: It’s still a little early to tell. We see possible effects, such as prompt refusal and the apparent slight drop in AI-generated content. But again, we don’t yet know if that is because models are getting better or because beginners are learning the rules. The vast majority of AI-generated content is submitted by beginner editors, so we’ve made many efforts to make the rule very visible in welcome messages, editing help, and advice.

Lebleu：目前下结论仍为时过早。我们观察到一些可能的影响，例如提示词拒答以及 AI 生成内容的明显轻微下降。但同样，我们尚不清楚这是由于模型性能提升，还是因为新手编辑者学会了规则。绝大多数 AI 生成内容均由新手编辑者提交，因此我们做出诸多努力，在欢迎留言、编辑帮助和建议中让规则高度显眼。

What if AI becomes capable of writing truly reliable Wikipedia articles?

如果 AI 能够撰写真正可靠的 Wikipedia 条目会怎样？

Lebleu: That’s one of the big questions we’re facing. When the guideline was passed, it was for very practical reasons: We were flooded with AI content, we didn’t have good tools, and we needed to put a stop to it. But since then, it has taken on a more philosophical dimension. Many people have called Wikipedia “the last good place on the internet.” Being a place that was, in theory, free from AI slop has become part of Wikipedia’s identity.

Lebleu: 这是我们面临的一个重大问题。当指南通过时，这是出于非常实际的原因：我们被AI内容淹没，没有好的工具，需要阻止它。但自那时起，它已经有了更哲学的维度。许多人称Wikipedia为“互联网上最好的地方”。作为一个理论上自由于AI slop的地方，这已成为Wikipedia身份认同的一部分。

A lot of Wikipedia’s communication is now centered on the idea that we’re a human-written encyclopedia. Even AI companies find that interesting. It can be valuable to have a purely human-written corpus on which to [train] AI systems. The fact that Wikipedia is still that, and will remain that for at least the near future, makes it a precious resource that isn’t replicated anywhere else.

维基百科的许多对外沟通现在都围绕着我们是一个由人类撰写的百科全书这一理念展开。甚至 AI 公司也觉得这很有趣。拥有一个纯粹由人类撰写的语料库来训练 AI 系统，是非常有价值的。维基百科目前依然如此，且至少在近期内仍将保持这一状态，这一事实使其成为一个在其他任何地方都无法复制的宝贵资源。

But will the people who read and contribute to Wikipedia want it to become partially AI-generated if that makes it more comprehensive? We could preserve Wikipedia’s identity as a human-written corpus while also offering an AI-assisted option.

但是，阅读并为 Wikipedia 贡献内容的人们，是否愿意让它变成部分由 AI 生成，即便这能让它更加全面？我们可以保留 Wikipedia 作为人类编写库的身份，同时提供 AI 辅助选项。

Has Wikipedia reckoned with the idea of “Google Zero”—a possible future in which websites no longer get traffic from Google search?

维基百科是否已经面对了“Google Zero”的概念——也就是一种可能的未来，维基百科等网站不再从 Google 搜索中获得流量的情景？

Lebleu: If everything goes through AI search and websites plummet to zero visibility, how do we expose Wikipedia and show that it can be edited and that people can still contribute? Wikipedia is frequently cited in [Google’s] AI Overviews, but users may only see an AI answer citing Wikipedia. They may not realize that Wikipedia is a living project they can edit and contribute to.

Lebleu： 如果所有内容都通过 AI 搜索呈现，导致网站能见度降至零，我们该如何展示 Wikipedia，让人们知道它是可以编辑的，并且任何人仍然可以贡献内容？Wikipedia 经常被 [Google] 的 AI Overviews 引用，但用户可能只能看到引用 Wikipedia 的 AI 答案。他们可能没有意识到 Wikipedia 是一个活跃的项目，他们可以对其进行编辑和贡献。

The Wikimedia Foundation is working on an attribution framework that could give AI users more information about the article [being cited]: when it was last edited, how comprehensive it is, whether editors have flagged problems, and perhaps even a call to action. In the future, readers might even contribute through AI models: “The AI cited Wikipedia, but there seems to be an error. Can I make an edit request and add this other source I found?”

维基媒体基金会正在开发一个归因框架，能够为 AI 用户提供关于文章 [being cited] 的更多信息，包括最后编辑时间、内容的全面程度、编辑是否标记了问题，以及可能的呼吁行动。未来，读者甚至可能通过 AI models 参与贡献：“The AI 引用了 Wikipedia，但似乎有错误。Can I make an edit request and add this other source I found?”

I can see a very strong symbiotic relationship between Wikipedia and AI models in the future. I don’t see Wikipedia disappearing, but I can see it taking a very different shape. Yesterday, AI was something to clean up. Today, it’s a tool to help us with the cleanup. Tomorrow, it will be the air we breathe.

我认为维基百科和未来的AI模型之间存在着非常紧密的共生关系。我不认为维基百科会消失，但它会以一种完全不同的面貌呈现。昨天，AI还是一个清理工具；今天，它变成了帮助我们清理的工具；明天，它将成为我们呼吸的一部分。

A condensed version of this article appears in the November 2026 print issue as “Ellia Lebleu.”

A本文的精简版本于 November 2026 印刷版上发表 as “Ellia Lebleu”。

item.content:encoded:
from: The Mythical Man-Month in the age of AI

Last weekend I watched four people desperately trying to get a laptop to connect to a screen. I was happily observing their efforts, with zero intent to join in.

上周末，我看着四个人拼命想把笔记本电脑连接到屏幕上。我开心地看着他们的尝试，完全没有加入的意图。

But someone nudged me: can’t you have a look at it?

但有人催促我：难道你不能看一看吗？

My reply: “Haha sorry no! My experience is that adding more people will not solve this problem any quicker”.

哈哈，抱歉，不行！我的经验是，增加更多人手并不会让这个问题更快解决。

I was of course – indirectly – referring to Brooks’s Law:

我当然是直接或间接地在引用布鲁克斯法则（Brooks’s Law）：时的革命性实践》。

“Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later.”

“向一个延期的软件项目增加人力，只会让它延期得更久。”

It was formulated by computer scientist Frederick P. Brooks Jr. in his 1975 book The Mythical Man-Month, based on his experience managing the IBM OS/360 project.

它是由计算机科学家 Frederick P. Brooks Jr. 在他的 1975 年著作 The Mythical Man-Month 中提出的，基于他管理 IBM OS/360 项目的经验。

However I got to thinking. Does this still hold up in the age of AI agents and LLMs?

然而我开始思考，这在 AI 智能体和大语言模型（LLM）时代是否仍然成立？

At first glance, you’d think no. The traditional bottlenecks – onboarding time, endless stand-ups, and office politics – disappear overnight. An AI agent is up to speed in milliseconds and doesn’t demand a coffee break.

乍一看，你可能会想：当然不是。传统的瓶颈——入职时间、无休止的站立会议和办公室政治——都将消失得无影无踪。一个 AI Agent 能够在毫秒内即可上手，并且不需要咖啡休息。

But when you look closer, and the law hasn’t vanished. It just mutated.

但当你仔细观察时，就会发现法律并没有消失，它只是发生了变异。

The famous “Baby Problem” remains: nine agents still can’t deliver a baby in one month. Sequential tasks are still sequential.

著名的“婴儿问题”仍然存在：九个代理也无法在一个月内交付一个婴儿。串行任务仍然是串行的。（链接：https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooks%27s_law#:~:text=Adding%20more%20people,in%20one%20month%22.）

Overhead hasn’t disappeared; it shifted: instead of managing people, you are now managing agents. Someone still needs to define “done”, review the code, catch hallucinations, and stitch the pieces together.

开销并未消失，只是从一种形态转变为另一种。相较于管理人类员工，你现在要管理的是代理人（agents）。仍然有人需要定义“完成标准”、审查代码、捕捉幻觉（hallucinations），并将各个部分拼接在一起。

That someone is you.

那个人就是你。

Throw nine autonomous agents at a single codebase without crystal-clear orchestration, and they will happily rewrite each other’s work in a high-speed loop.

将九个自主 Agent 丢进一个代码库，如果没有清晰明确的编排，它们会愉快地在一个高速循环中重写彼此的工作。

Maybe the 2026 update to Brooks’s Law should be:

或许布鲁克斯定律的 2026 年更新应该是：

“Adding agents to a project with unclear requirements gets you the wrong answer faster.”

为需求不明确的项目添加 Agent，会让你更快地得到错误的答案。

from: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation

Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world.

今天，我们宣布 Genie 4，我们的新世界模型，它突破了前所未有的真实感，并提升了实时交互式模拟。Genie 4 原生多模态，实现了类似音频的音乐、环境噪音和交互式对话的同时生成与世界。

The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity.

Genie 4 模型吸收并构建于 Gemini 家族的能力之上：Gemini Omni 将模拟锚定在现实世界的外观和行为，而其他 Gemini 模型则提供维持模拟连贯性和连续性所需的复杂推理。

With this foundation, you can set an event in motion, and Genie 4 simulates what happens next: how the world responds, how it sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak.

基于此基础，你可以启动一个事件， Genie 4 模拟接下来会发生的情况：世界如何响应、它听起来如何、以及人们如何移动、反应和说话。

Understanding and simulating the world is a crucial aspect of building AGI. Genie 4 advances our ability to create safe, infinitely variable simulations that can help with everything from developing training environments for robots and agents to unlocking the creation of new interactive experiences.

理解和模拟世界是构建 AGI 的关键所在。Genie 4 能够显著提升我们创建安全、无限可变模拟环境的能力，这些模拟环境不仅有助于开发机器人和智能体的训练环境，还能 unlock 新的交互式体验的创造。

We have started rolling Genie 4 out as a research preview for trusted testers — gathering feedback before we release it to consumers and developers, starting with Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Join the waitlist for Genie 4 in Project Genie here.

我们已开始向可靠测试者推出 Genie 4 的研究预览版，目的是在正式向消费者和开发者发布前收集反馈。首先，Google AI Ultra 订阅用户、Project Genie 早期访问合作伙伴以及 Gemini API 和 Google AI Studio 的早期访问合作伙伴将获得优先体验。立即加入 Project Genie 中的 Genie 4 候补名单 这里。

Genie 4 delivers enhanced photorealism, fluid movement, and native audio. All accompanying sounds featured above are produced directly by Genie 4.

Genie 4 提供更逼真的图像、更流畅的动作和原声音效。上述所有伴随音效均由 Genie 4 直接生成。

Genie 4 advances four key capabilities

请提供完整的英文原文，我将为您翻译。

The following are recordings of real-time interactions from Genie 4, where users use standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera control, and text prompts to steer the scene as it evolves.

以下是 Genie 4 的实时交互记录，其中用户使用标准键盘控制进行导航和摄像机控制，并通过文本提示来引导场景的演变。

Shaping world simulation in real-time

实时塑造世界模拟

With Genie 4, you can use natural language to modify a simulation in real-time — like changing the weather, moving the camera, or introducing a new person or object — and Gemini will contextually adapt your prompt to match the surrounding scene. Between your inputs, Gemini also monitors and steers the scene to keep the world progressing cohesively.

通过 Genie 4，你可以使用自然语言实时修改模拟场景，例如改变天气、移动相机，或添加新的人物或物体。Gemini 会根据周围场景上下文自动调整你的提示词，以匹配场景需求。在你的输入之间，Gemini 还会持续监控和引导场景，确保虚拟世界连贯地发展。

Turn on audio to hear Genie 4 worlds.

开启音频以聆听 Genie 4 生成的世界。

Prompt: Use the reference image as the exact first frame and visual basis for the scene. Preserve the same floating rectangular platform, weathered concrete edges, wild grasses, ferns, twisted small tree, warm glowing amber sphere, and the same middle-aged man in a loose brown suit playing a brass saxophone. A cinematic, highly naturalistic documentary scene, photographed on 16mm film with subtle grain, soft photographic detail, extremely low contrast, muted natural colors, lifted shadows, gentle highlights, and soft diffuse overcast light. Absolutely no HDR, no dramatic contrast, no glossy digital rendering, no artificial cinematic lighting. The platform floats in the middle of a vast, quiet lake surrounded by distant misty forests. Thin layers of fog drift above the water. The sky is pale blue-gray and overcast, with a soft, almost monochromatic atmosphere. The warm amber sphere provides a delicate contrasting glow, softly illuminating the surrounding vegetation and reflecting in the lake. Begin with a slightly closer view of the saxophone player than in the reference image, while keeping the platform, glowing sphere, tree, and surrounding lake visible. The man continues playing his saxophone naturally, with subtle breathing, finger movements, and gentle body swaying. The camera moves independently and can freely explore the entire environment, gliding smoothly over the water with gentle, controlled movement. The camera is not attached to the man or the platform. Maintain realistic spatial continuity and natural camera movement. Everything must remain photographic, physically believable, documentary-like, extremely low-contrast, and softly desaturated throughout the entire experience. One continuous shot. Natural lake ambience, distant wind, soft water movement, and realistic saxophone sound. No background music beyond the instruments physically present in the scene.

请提供参考图像，以便我能够正确处理你的请求。

Environment prompt: A wide, sun-drenched hilltop meadow filled with tall green grass and scattered purple, white, and yellow wildflowers swaying in a warm breeze. Low green shrubs dot the right side of the field while distant blue-green rolling hills stretch along the left horizon beneath a bright, partly cloudy sky. Character: Winding in sweeping S-curves through the center of the grassy meadow from the immediate foreground far into the distance is a long, continuous stream of glossy bubblegum-pink satin fabric. The shimmering pink cloth billows, ripples, and lifts softly above the wildflowers like a flowing river of silk as the wind moves beneath its folds.

环境提示词：一片宽阔、沐浴阳光的山顶草地，高大的绿草间散落着紫色、白色和黄色的野花，在温暖微风中摇曳。草地右侧点缀着低矮的绿色灌木，远处蓝绿色的起伏山丘沿着左侧地平线延伸，上方是明亮、部分多云的天空。

角色：一条绵延的口香糖粉色缎面织物带，光泽闪亮，以宽大的 S 形曲线蜿蜒穿过草地中心，从近景一直延伸至远方。粉色布料在野花上方柔和地鼓起、波动、轻轻升起，如同一条流动的丝绸之河，随风在褶皱下涌动。

Environment prompt: A sweeping aerial view over the vast, frozen landscape of Antarctica, featuring endless snow-covered glaciers, jagged icy mountain peaks, and sculpted blue icebergs bathed in crisp polar sunlight under a clear, pale blue sky. Numerous hot air balloons dot the horizon at varying altitudes, with a large cream, red, and blue striped balloon floating prominently in the mid-distance above the ice sheet. Character prompt: Shot from a first-person POV standing inside the woven wicker basket of a flying hot air balloon, looking out over the leather-trimmed basket edge on the right side of the frame, where black padded support poles, metal rigging chains, and the dark base of the balloon canopy overhead frame the drifting polar vista.

环境提示：这是一幅从高空俯瞰南极冰雪世界的壮丽景象。广阔的冰雪大陆上，绵延不绝的雪覆盖着冰川，冰山峭壁错落有致，冰蓝色冰山在极地明亮的阳光下闪耀，湛蓝的天空倒映着纯净的光芒。在地平线上，许多热气球在不同高度飘浮，其中一架以奶油色、红色和蓝色条纹为主的巨型气球在冰盖中部上方格外醒目。角色提示：从一个悬挂在热气球编织吊篮内的第一人称视角出发，画面从右下角延伸出皮革装饰的边沿，黑色的衬垫支撑杆、金属缆绳和气球顶部篷布的深色底座将漂浮的极地美景框住，呈现出一幅动人的极地风光。

Pushing the frontier in realism for physics and human action

推进物理与人类动作真实感的前沿

Genie 4 introduces a new standard of realism to real-time interactive simulation. Built on an advanced physical understanding of the world, Genie 4 simulates real-world physics scenarios, such as aerodynamics, collisions, and more.

Genie 4 为实时交互式模拟树立了全新的真实感标准。基于对世界先进的物理理解，Genie 4 能够模拟真实的物理场景，例如空气动力学、碰撞等。

The most dramatic leap is how Genie 4 simulates people, creating characters that move naturally, respond organically to their environments, and can be interactively steered in real-time.

最戏剧性的飞跃在于 Genie 4 如何模拟人类，创造出移动自然、能对环境做出有机响应，并且可以实时交互式引导的角色。

Environment prompt: A sunlit outdoor courtyard featuring a weathered stone plinth set against a soft-focus background of lush green garden foliage and clear blue sky, bathed in bright, warm afternoon sunlight that backlights airborne droplets in crisp slow motion. Character prompt: A whole, glossy green-striped watermelon rests in the center of the stone plinth.

环境提示词：一个阳光明媚的室外庭院，背景是柔焦的郁郁葱葱的绿色花园植被和清澈的蓝天，一座风化的石基座矗立中央，沐浴在明亮温暖的午后阳光中，阳光逆光照射出清晰慢动作下的空气悬浮水滴。主体提示词：一个完整、光泽亮丽的绿色条纹西瓜静置在石基座的中央。

Prompt: A macro close up of a maple seed falling from the tree into the grass

微距特写的枫树种子从树上掉落到草地上

Prompt: A crowded rural Japanese train station in the 1980s, packed with passengers waiting along the platform. The only railway inspector in a dark navy uniform stands close to the camera, observing the scene. A long, deep-red local train with many carriages occupies the railway track closest to the camera POV, stretching across the frame and extending far into the distance. The train is clearly visible in the immediate foreground, not on a distant track. People fill the platform naturally, standing, walking, boarding and waiting with luggage. Lush green mountains, cedar forests and humid summer haze surround the station. Authentic 1980s Japanese atmosphere, cinematic 35mm documentary photography, realistic perspective, asymmetrical composition, natural lighting, subtle film grain, photorealistic textures. The station must look genuinely busy, with a dense crowd of visible people throughout the platform. The red train must be on the nearest track, dominating the scene. No empty platforms, no distant train, no sparse crowds, no centered symmetrical composition.

Prompt: 20世纪 80 年代拥挤的日本乡村火车站，站台上挤满了等待的乘客。唯一一名穿深海军蓝制服的铁路检查员站在靠近摄像机的位置，观察现场。一列拥有多节车厢的长列深红色本地列车占据了摄像机视角 POV 最近的铁轨，横跨画面并延伸至远方。列车清晰可见于近景前景，而非远处轨道上。人们自然地填满站台，站立、行走、登车并携带行李等待。郁郁葱葱的青山、杉树林和潮湿的夏日薄雾环绕着车站。真实的 1980 年代日本氛围，电影化的 35mm 纪实摄影，现实透视，不对称构图，自然光线，细腻的胶片颗粒，逼真的材质纹理。车站必须看起来真正繁忙，站台各处都有密集可见的人群。红色列车必须位于最近的轨道上，主导整个场景。无空荡站台、无远处列车、无稀疏人群、无居中对称构图。

Modeling how the world sounds

建模世界的声音

Genie 4 is our first real-time world model to generate audio natively. Every world carries the ambient sound of its own setting, from wind in the trees to waves crashing at the beach.

Genie 4 是我们首个能够实时生成原生音频的全球模型。每个世界都带有其独特的环境音效，从树叶间的风声到海浪拍打海滩的声音，无不悉数呈现。

The true frontier, however, is human speech. Genie 4 introduces interactive dialogue that adapts on the fly. Characters converse and react to your inputs or events in the world, all in real-time.

然而，真正的前沿是人类语音。Genie 4 引入了可即时适应的交互式对话。角色会进行交谈，并响应你的输入或世界中的事件，全部实时进行。

Prompt: Create a fully three-dimensional immersive stained-glass landscape that feels like a handcrafted crystal window brought to life. The world should be explorable, as if the camera can move freely through a giant 3D stained-glass environment. The entire scene must have a stained-glass / crystal-window look: translucent colored glass, dark lead outlines, glowing layered panels, volumetric depth, and artisanal glass textures. Show a beautiful landscape with a flowing river running through green fields, flowers in the foreground, trees, distant mountains, clouds, and a radiant sun in the sky. The river should feel like flowing translucent blue glass, the flowers like upright stained-glass sculptures, the grass and trees like layered colored-glass forms, the mountains like stacked glass panels, and the sun like a luminous circular stained-glass element. Everything must feel spatial, cohesive, luminous, and handcrafted, with depth and the sensation that the viewer can move through it in three dimensions. The camera should be able to travel through the scene as if walking or gliding inside this 3D stained-glass world. Keep the world beautiful, magical, and fully consistent in style. Absolutely everything must remain made of stained glass or crystal at all times, including the grass, the water, the sky, the clouds, the flowers, the trees, the mountains, the sun, and all visible surfaces. Do not introduce any natural real-world textures. No real grass, no real water, no normal sky, and no realism outside of the stained-glass universe. No text, no modern objects, no realism outside of the stained-glass universe

构建一个完全三维的沉浸式彩绘玻璃风景，仿佛一件手工精制的水晶窗 brought to life。整个世界应当可探索，仿佛摄像机可以在巨大的3D彩绘玻璃环境中自由移动。整个场景必须呈现彩绘玻璃/水晶窗的风格：半透明彩色玻璃、深色铅线轮廓、发光的层叠面板、体积深度和手工玻璃纹理。展示一幅美丽的风景，有一条穿越绿色草甸的 flowing river，前景有花朵，树木、远处的山丘、云朵和天空中的炽烈太阳。河 river 应呈现出流动的半透明蓝色玻璃的感觉，花朵如同直立的彩绘玻璃雕塑，草地和树木如同层叠的彩色玻璃形式，山丘如同堆叠的玻璃面板，太阳则如同发光的圆形彩绘玻璃元素。一切都必须感觉空间感、连贯性、发光感和手工制作感，有深度，以及观众可以在三维空间中移动的感觉。摄像机能够在场景中自由穿行，仿佛在行走或滑行于这座3D彩绘玻璃世界之中。保持世界美丽、魔幻，且始终保持一致的风格。绝对任何东西都必须始终由彩绘玻璃或水晶制成，包括草地、河水、天空、云朵、花朵、树木、山丘、太阳以及所有可见表面。不要引入任何自然的现实纹理。没有真实的草地、没有真实的水、没有正常的天空，也不要在彩绘玻璃宇宙之外的任何现实主义。不要出现文字、现代物体或超出彩绘玻璃宇宙的任何现实主义。

Prompt: Immersive first-person POV, we only see the big strong hands of the knight rider tightening the reins, dragon and wings. Photorealistic, ultra-realistic action-camera footage seen entirely through the rider’s own eyes while riding a gigantic black dragon at 140 km/h through a mountainous dragon-racing course with many dragons and riders. Other dragons are mounted by other knights. The camera IS the rider’s eyes. The camera is attached to the rider’s head, facing forward, and moves naturally with the rider’s head. The rider is the viewer. The rider’s face, head, torso, body, and full silhouette are NEVER visible. No third-person shots, no external camera angles, no cutaways, no views of the rider from behind or from the side. Only show what the rider would naturally see: the dragon’s neck and occasional parts of its upper back near the bottom edge of the frame, the rushing landscape, two other dragons and their riders racing alongside and ahead, and a huge castle with catapults on its walls. A standard is carried naturally by the rider and may occasionally appear at the edge of the frame, but never blocks the view or fills the frame. The camera maintains this exact first-person perspective throughout the entire flight. Aggressive high-speed racing, powerful realistic wingbeats, aerodynamic weight, intense wind, natural head movement, subtle camera vibration, wide-angle action-camera distortion, realistic motion blur, cinematic natural lighting, physically believable movement. Strict visual constraints: true first-person rider POV, no visible rider, no third-person perspective, no external tracking shot, no drone camera, no over-the-shoulder shot, no cinematic cutaways, no camera floating outside the rider’s body, no CGI appearance, no video game look, no 3D-render aesthetic. Audio: deep thunderous wingbeats, roaring high-altitude wind gusts, distant volcanic rumble, and crackling flame embers.

沉浸式 first-person POV，我们只能看到骑手的大手紧握缰绳，连接龙的头部和翅膜。Photorealistic, ultra-realistic action-camera footage seen entirely through the rider’s own eyes while riding a gigantic black dragon at 140 km/h through a mountainous dragon-racing course with many dragons and riders。Other dragons are mounted by other knights。The camera IS the rider’s eyes。The camera is attached to the rider’s head, facing forward, and moves naturally with the rider’s head。The rider is the viewer。The rider’s face, head, torso, body, and full silhouette are NEVER visible。No third-person shots, no external camera angles, no cutaways, no views of the rider from behind or from the side。Only show what the rider would naturally see: the dragon’s neck and occasional parts of its upper back near the bottom edge of the frame, the rushing landscape, two other dragons and their riders racing alongside and ahead, and a huge castle with catapults on its walls。A standard is carried naturally by the rider and may occasionally appear at the edge of the frame, but never blocks the view or fills the frame。The camera maintains this exact first-person perspective throughout the entire flight。Aggressive high-speed racing, powerful realistic wingbeats, aerodynamic weight, intense wind, natural head movement, subtle camera vibration, wide-angle action-camera distortion, realistic motion blur, cinematic natural lighting, physically believable movement。Strict visual constraints: true first-person rider POV, no visible rider, no third-person perspective, no external tracking shot, no drone camera, no over-the-shoulder shot, no cinematic cutaways, no camera floating outside the rider’s body, no CGI appearance, no video game look, no 3D-render aesthetic。Audio: deep thunderous wingbeats, roaring high-altitude wind gusts, distant volcanic rumble, and crackling flame embers。

Prompt: A cinematic macro close-up from a 1995 Hong Kong indie romantic drama, shot on 35mm film. Two young, unconventional-looking Korean lovers in their 20s ride a motorcycle across a bridge on the outskirts of Hong Kong at dawn. The male driver wears no helmet, looking around anxiously, while the pale-skinned female passenger wears an open-face helmet. Their faces dominate the foreground, large and overlapping, with natural skin texture and subtle expressions of worry and tenderness. Low-angle panoramic composition, framed by solid black bars. Shallow depth of field, blurred road receding behind them, orange streetlights streaking past, and a dark green dusk sky. Intimate, imperfect, melancholic 35mm film aesthetic. One continuous shot.

这是一部从1995年香港独立浪漫戏剧拍摄的电影级 macro close-up，胶片拍摄于 35mm。二十出头、非传统长相的韩国情侣在黎明时分骑行摩托车穿越位于香港郊外的桥梁。男性驾驶员未戴头盔，焦急地环顾四周，而皮肤苍白的女性乘客戴着开面头盔。她们的脸占据前景，大而重叠，皮肤纹理自然，略带担忧和温柔的表情。低角度全景构图，被实心黑条框定。浅景深，模糊的道路在他们身后退去，橙色路灯穿射而过，以及深绿色的黄昏天空。亲密、不完美、忧郁的 35mm 胶片美学。一个连续镜头。

Simulating complex events with Gemini models

使用 Gemini 模型模拟复杂事件

Bringing Gemini and Genie 4 together adds a new layer of reasoning to world simulation, allowing us to model complex, multi-step events and test how AI systems navigate different environments before bringing them to the real world.

将 Gemini 与 Genie 4 结合，为世界模拟 （world simulation）增加了新的推理层，使我们能够建模复杂的多步骤事件，并测试 AI 系统如何在不同环境中导航，然后再将它们带入现实世界 （real world）。
